## Buy a House After Bankruptcy in Wisconsin [2026]: Waiting Periods + WI DPA
Source: https://buyahouseafterbankruptcy.com/states/wisconsin.html

← buyahouseafterbankruptcy.com home

Buy a House After Bankruptcy in Wisconsin [2026]: Waiting Periods + WI DPA

State-specific rules, federal court data, and practical guidance for Wisconsin residents.

Buying a Home After Bankruptcy in Wisconsin - Federal Waiting Periods

Waiting periods are federal and apply uniformly in Wisconsin. The state-specific layer is down-payment assistance and homestead protection, not the underlying loan program.

Loan TypeAfter Chapter 7After Chapter 13

FHA2 years from discharge1 year of on-time plan payments + court permission

VA2 years from discharge1 year of on-time plan payments + court permission

USDA3 years from discharge1 year of on-time plan payments + court permission

Conventional (Fannie/Freddie)4 years from discharge (2 years with extenuating circumstances)2 years from discharge or 4 years from dismissal

Jumbo (non-conforming)7 years typical7 years typical

"Extenuating circumstances" (job loss, medical event, divorce) can reduce waiting periods. See FHA guide and conventional mortgage guide.

Wisconsin Down-Payment Assistance Programs

WHEDA (Wisconsin Housing and Economic Development Authority) Easy Close Advantage ($6,000 DPA, 0% deferred).

These state-level programs are compatible with post-bankruptcy borrowers who meet the federal waiting period. Key considerations for Wisconsin DPA:

First-time buyer requirement. "First time" is usually defined as no home ownership in the past 3 years. A prior bankruptcy does not restart this clock; selling the home pre-petition can.

Income limits. Most Wisconsin DPA is capped by household income (typically 80-140% of area median income).

Credit minimums. Wisconsin DPA generally requires 620-640 minimum credit score; rebuilding after bankruptcy is the path.

Purchase price caps. Wisconsin DPA programs cap purchase prices by county.

Homebuyer education. Most Wisconsin DPA requires 8-hour HUD-approved homebuyer education class (separate from bankruptcy credit counseling).

Owner-occupancy. Must be primary residence, not investment or second home.

See down-payment assistance overview.

Rebuilding Credit in Wisconsin

Credit-rebuild is the rate-limiting step for most post-bankruptcy Wisconsin homebuyers. A typical Wisconsin rebuild arc:

Month 0-6: Secured credit card ($200-$500 deposit); automatic payment to utilities; begin tracking FICO monthly.

Month 6-12: Second tradeline (credit-builder loan or authorized user); target 580+ FICO.

Month 12-24: Unsecured card graduation; auto loan if needed (rate will be poor, focus on on-time payment history); target 620+ FICO.

Month 24-36: Target 640+ FICO for Wisconsin DPA eligibility; build 3 tradelines with 12+ months of on-time history.

Month 36-48: At 4-year mark (conventional) or earlier (FHA/VA), meet waiting-period and credit minimums simultaneously.

See credit rebuild guide.

Wisconsin Homestead Exemption - Why It Matters Before You Buy

Wisconsin homestead exemption: $75,000 ($150,000 joint) (Wis. Stat. 815.20).

The Wisconsin homestead exemption protects equity in your primary residence from most creditors. It is most relevant before you file bankruptcy (to plan equity below the exemption cap) but also matters for post-discharge planning:

Equity headroom. If the Wisconsin homestead exemption is generous (Wisconsin is capped at $75,000), you have flexibility for home appreciation without equity-stripping risk.

Future financial shocks. If you face another financial crisis post-discharge, the Wisconsin homestead protects equity up to the exemption amount.

Judgment liens. Wisconsin judgment creditors may file liens against your post-discharge home for non-dischargeable debts (DSO, fraud, some taxes).

See Wisconsin full exemption list.

Many Wisconsin homebuyers arriving at the mortgage-qualification conversation have a prior bankruptcy discharge. These FJC numbers show Wisconsin's bankruptcy resolution context.

Chapter 13 is often overlooked as a path to post-bankruptcy homeownership. The federal rule: after 1 year of on-time Chapter 13 plan payments, FHA and VA allow mortgage qualification during the plan - with court permission.

In Wisconsin, this is a real pathway. Ask your Chapter 13 trustee whether they have a standard "motion to incur debt" template. See FAQ on in-plan mortgages.
